common_name: Carpet Angel Shasta Daisy (AAS-Winning Groundcover Leucanthemum)
subcategory: AAS Perennial Winner groundcover shasta daisy

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants or divisions in spring after the last hard frost, or in fall in milder zones, into well-drained soil in full sun to part sun.

directions: Carpet Angel is an AAS Perennial Winner recognized as the first true groundcover-type Shasta daisy, forming a dense, low mat only 4 to 6 inches tall while spreading up to 20 inches wide. From spring through fall it is topped with abundant 3-inch, semi-double white daisies that open a frilly inner row of petals around the gold center, a shape AAS judges singled out as unlike any other Shasta daisy on the market. Plant divisions or container starts in full sun to part sun in well-drained soil, spacing plants 18 to 20 inches apart to let the mat knit together as a flowering groundcover or container trailer. It needs no staking, tolerates winter cold reliably through USDA zone 4, and benefits from occasional deadheading to keep the long bloom season going.

common_name: Sweet Daisy Birdy Shasta Daisy (AAS-Winning Early-Blooming Leucanthemum)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring once hard frost has passed, into rich, organic, evenly moist soil in full sun.

directions: Sweet Daisy Birdy is an AAS Perennial Winner selected for producing large, 5-inch reflexed white daisies with ruffled, feathery petal tips around a golden-yellow button center, opening earlier in the season than comparison Shasta daisies. Upright plants reach 18 to 24 inches tall and are hardy from USDA zone 3 to 10, tolerating both harsh winters and summer heat better than many older Shasta daisy cultivars. Space plants roughly 3 feet apart in rich, organic, evenly moist soil in full sun, where the sturdy stems need no staking and make excellent cut flowers. Deadheading is optional but encourages continued bloom, and the dark green foliage stays attractive through the growing season.

planting.note: Sow seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, pressing it into the mix or covering only lightly with vermiculite, then transplant out after the last frost into full to partial sun.

directions: Twizzle Purple is an AAS regional winner (Heartland and Southeast) selected for its compact, uniformly branched habit and profuse display of inch-long, tubular purple flowers from late spring into summer. Sow seed in small pots, pressing it into the mix or covering only lightly with vermiculite, and keep the medium at about 65F; germination takes 2 to 3 weeks, with seedlings ready to move to larger pots after another 6 to 8 weeks of growth. Set plants 10 to 14 inches apart in full to partial sun and well-drained, lean to average soil, where established clumps prove fairly drought tolerant and reliably winter hardy from USDA zone 5 to 8. Deadhead spent flower spikes to prolong bloom, and expect hummingbirds and bees to visit regularly.

planting.note: Start seed indoors well ahead of the last frost date and transplant out once frost danger has passed, into full sun and well-drained soil.

directions: Arabesque Red is an AAS National Winner selected from Penstemon hartwegii for its large, bell-shaped, red-and-white bicolor flowers held on upright, well-branched stems from summer to frost. Plants reach 18 to 24 inches tall and about as wide, performing best in full sun and well-drained soil with weekly watering and a monthly feeding of controlled-release or liquid fertilizer through the growing season. It is heat tolerant and hardy from USDA zone 6 to 9, needs no staking despite its height, and draws hummingbirds and butterflies over a long bloom season. Deadhead spent flower spikes to keep new buds coming, and start seed indoors well ahead of the last frost date since this hybrid penstemon is typically grown and sold as a flowering nursery transplant.
